stances.claim: The Supreme Court's Aug 30, 2022 TRO on NCAP is legally correct, though issued ex parte, because the two petitions' sworn allegations of three constitutional violations are cogent and facially valid: due-process deprivation, penalization of the registered owner (a non-participant) instead of the actual driver, and a Data Privacy Act breach enabling public exposure of owner data via a plate-number lookup.

Well-settled jurisprudence grants courts sound discretion to halt continued transgressions immediately when sworn allegations of constitutional rights violations appear facially truthful and valid -- provided the halt does not cause irremediable damage to public interest.

The TRO is legally proper because the petitions show irreparable injury from continued enforcement, and under the Rules of Court a TRO is meant precisely to protect substantial rights and prevent continuous irremediable injury pending full hearing.

The TRO is temporary and not a prejudgment of the final decision -- the SC may revoke, modify, or change it moto proprio if the respondents' 10-day non-extendible Comment or the Jan 24, 2023 Oral Arguments show fallacy in petitioners' allegations or a more overriding public interest.

Solicitor General Menardo I. Guevarra -- distinguished nonpartisan DOJ Secretary in the Duterte administration and P-Noy deputy executive secretary for legal affairs -- is a well-respected counsel for the LTO, and this will be his first 'baptism of fire' as the tribune of the people.

NCAP's laudable intentions -- discipline, minimizing physical-apprehension corruption, digitalization -- must still be accomplished within the rule of law; autocratic shortcuts in violation of basic rights are abhorred in democratic societies, for 'the road to hell is paved with good intentions.'

notable_anecdotes: The Juman Paa plate-number demonstration -- that anyone can type a plate number into the LGU's NCAP website and view the registered owner's name, address, and number of violations -- turning an abstract privacy claim into a concrete demonstrable test.

The personnel-credit paragraph for SolGen Menardo I. Guevarra -- distinguished nonpartisan DOJ Sec in Duterte administration and P-Noy deputy executive secretary for legal affairs -- paired with the gentle 'baptism of fire' framing, modeling CJ's habit of professional warmth even when the institutional client (LTO) is on the losing side of the TRO.
The 'right way to do the right thing at the right time by the right person and for the right reasons' five-Rs aphorism -- a quintessentially CJ-style framework-as-aphorism device.
The closing adage -- 'the road to hell is paved with good intentions' -- invoked not as cliché but as the encapsulation of the column's ends-vs-means rule-of-law argument.

The non-participant framing of penalty under NCAP -- 'punishes a non-participant, an innocent person in an alleged crime' -- collapsing the entire vehicle-registration-vs-driver-identity critique into a single sentence.

one_paragraph_summary: Defending the Supreme Court's Aug 30, 2022 temporary restraining order on the no-contact apprehension policy (NCAP) -- which halted implementation by the LGUs of Manila, Quezon City, Valenzuela, Parañaque, and Muntinlupa under an MMDA Resolution dated Feb 16, 2016, and barred the LTO from sharing motorist information -- Panganiban explains why the TRO is both legally correct and legally proper. Although issued ex parte, it rests on the petitions' cogent sworn allegations of three constitutional violations: NCAP denies due process by not allowing alleged violators sufficient time to contest before penalty; it oppressively penalizes the registered owner of the vehicle (a non-participant, innocent person) instead of the actual driver; and it crosses the right to privacy because, as petitioner counsel Juman Paa demonstrated, anyone can type a plate number into the LGU website and view the owner's name, address, and violation history -- in violation of the Data Privacy Act. Well-settled jurisprudence grants courts sound discretion to halt such transgressions immediately when sworn allegations appear facially valid. The TRO is also procedurally proper to prevent irreparable injury pending full hearing, and is expressly temporary -- the SC may revoke, modify, or change it moto proprio if the respondents' 10-day non-extendible Comment, or the Jan 24, 2023 Oral Arguments, show fallacy in the petitions or a more overriding public interest. CJ welcomes new SolGen Menardo I. Guevarra -- distinguished nonpartisan DOJ Secretary under Duterte and deputy executive secretary for legal affairs under P-Noy -- to his 'baptism of fire' as the tribune of the people. He acknowledges NCAP's laudable intentions (discipline, anti-corruption, digitalization), but insists that 'there is a right way to do the right thing at the right time by the right person and for the right reasons' -- laudable purposes must be accomplished within the rule of law, because 'autocratic shortcuts done in violation of basic rights are abhorred in democratic societies, for as the adage goes, the road to hell is paved with good intentions.'
